title: Unpopular Opinion: AI is currently good enough to do AAA games end to end, but it's expensive...
author: my_btc_throwaway

comments.author: HupsuHusu
comments.body: Good times ahead. Now EA and Activision and others can just make Call of Duty 2027 January every month with AI and sack 95% of their developers. /s

replies.author: my_btc_throwaway
replies.body: I mean, the whole industry, the whole world, really, is in for a significant shake up. I know people compare it to the industrial revolution, but this is the first time in history its intelligence is being offloaded, and with the general nature of it, I don't see how it just doesn't cause riots ending with either guillotines or UBI.

replies.author: HupsuHusu
replies.body: I can totally agree with this. But you must understand that it is extremely hard to just trust your word when you make such a claim you did regarding AAA, without seeing what you achieved with that money. I can imagine what you say, because I can’t tell difference of real art vs chatgpt image (assuming it doesn’t have six finger people), or real song va Suno song. So you might be totally on something, I get that. But no gameplay, hard to say :)

comments.author: my_btc_throwaway
comments.body:
I would suggest reassessing your workflows and actually looking at what you can offload to AI, if it's taking you several weeks to get an asset ready you've got your hands too deep in the weeds. Get on the tractor, let the plow do the work.

Just today, I had 15 assets completed, concepts done, models done, textures done, rigging done, animations done (each one with 20+ animations). These aren't basic assets, these are fully fledged buildings and 3D characters. 

I'd recommend image references for your concepts, then tripo + opus 5.5 for the first model, then fable 5.2 to clean it up if its biological, if its non-biological, opus 5.5 can just build it in blender completely with gauntlet loops.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: I dont need to reassess, im a professional artist and i have high standards for my assets that AI just doesnt meet. It is helpful for some stuff there and i have built custom tools for Maya to help me with rigging for example and so on. But other than that i cant let AI do all these creative tasks. At best i can let AI do some technical parts of these works and even some creative parts but thats limited to certain background and prop assets. Concept art is also very important to be done by myself albeit i have AI involved for rapid prototyping and ideations which still dont replace me doing these things on my own either.

replies.author: my_btc_throwaway
replies.body: As I said earlier, it's up to you if you want to ride your horse to school when everyone else is driving cars. I appreciate you have a love for the game, but it sounds like you're not using frontier stuff. Fable 5.2 (use it on xhigh) which dropped last week, is genuinely rigging and animating models perfectly right now.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: I am already “driving a car”, one that is better than any car that people who rely on AI for these kind of tasks drive. Im using the best software for these tasks while taking advantage of AI where it doesnt sacrifice the quality of my work or not noticeably. And yes, i use Fable 5.2 for a variety of tasks within a limited scope due to its weekly allowance limits and the fact that i use Fable 5.2 outside of game development too.

replies.author: my_btc_throwaway
replies.body: Ask it to do more than, don't limit its scope. As I said, it's good enough to do it - it's just expensive. Correctly SOP the process, and you will see incredible results. If you want to hand craft it, go for it, tbh opus 5.5 xhigh is good enough for almost everything, fable 5.2 just really saturated animation and rigging though.

replies.author: _HoundOfJustice
replies.body: Sadly i see that you do not the reality of all these things and are either trolling with this account or just hoping to achieve what you want so you tell it yourself and to others that it is the way you wish it to be. I dont think a further discussion is worth it tbh.

replies.author: my_btc_throwaway
replies.body: Did you want to share more about what you're working on or your workflows? I'd be happy to give you a second pair of eyes to see if I can find where you might be able to improve efficiency

comments.author: NullzeroJP
comments.body: Cool, thanks for sharing! Yeah, I see a lot of people with custom pipelines and ticket systems. I keep wondering if I should roll my own or go with something like Linear or Paperclip or something... sometimes so tempting to work on the tools and dev environment that make the game, than the actual game itself. Its like a meta Factorio or something.

replies.author: my_btc_throwaway
replies.body: Yes!! Exactly, it's a constant battle because you're always optimizing it too. I'd definitely recommend just building your own version of linear, that's what I did. A single program that has every AI subscription, every computer, every ticket, and can make calls to any of them depending on workload. My plan is to reuse it for the next game, idea is already written down and ready to go. Just have to finish this one first!

comments.author: my_btc_throwaway
comments.body: i have 3x claude ultra and 1x openAI so around $1000 per month, inference-wise about $20k-$30k per month I guess at API prices. I expect this to be complete at around $100k of api prices.

comments.author: Tall_Illustrator5116
comments.body: I think we're seeing the biggest explosion of the dunning-kruger effect in history in real time, the sheer amount of ai derangement is crazy.
